issues.detail: The Greek 'εβουλομην' (eboulomen) is an imperfect verb expressing a desire or intention. The Vietnamese translation 'Ta cũng muốn nghe' (I also want to hear) misses the nuance of the imperfect tense which, in this context, suggests a continuous state of desire or a specific intent at that moment. However, more critically, the Greek 'ακουσαι' (akousai) is an aorist active infinitive, and 'ακουση' (akousē) is a future indicative. The Vietnamese translation treats these as simple present/future desires without capturing the specific grammatical movement from 'wanting to hear' to 'will hear'.

The Greek text says 'ακουσαι ο δε αυριον φησιν ακουση αυτου' (and he [Festus] said, 'tomorrow he will hear him'). The Vietnamese translation adds 'vua' (king) to refer to Festus. While Festus was a prefect, the Greek text does not use a title for him in this specific phrase; it simply uses 'αυτος' (he). Adding 'vua' is an addition not present in the Greek.
